biography: Jérémy Iglesias's journey began on the sun-drenched karting tracks of southern France. As a young boy, his grandfather, a retired mechanic, introduced him to the roar of engines and the thrill of speed. Jérémy wasn't content with casual laps; he disassembled and reassembled his kart countless times, learning the intricacies of its mechanics, and pushing its limits. His aggressive style quickly became his trademark, often bumping and grinding his way to the front. One defining moment came at the French National Karting Championship, where he recovered from a spin on the first lap to claw his way back to victory, showcasing his relentless determination. Now at his peak, Iglesias continues to compete in the Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter category, hungry for more victories and eager to prove he's a force to be reckoned with.
drivingStyle: Iglesias's driving style is characterized by controlled aggression. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and his willingness to dive into corners, often surprising his rivals with his audacious overtakes. While his aggressive approach can sometimes lead to collisions, his tire management is surprisingly adept. He's able to push hard early in a race, building a lead, and then subtly manage his tires to maintain his advantage in the closing laps. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at the 2018 European Karting Championship final. Bellini accused Iglesias of deliberately forcing him off the track, sparking a heated exchange that continues to simmer to this day.

careerHighlight: Winning the French National Karting Championship in 2019 after a dominant performance, securing his place as one of the top karting talents in France.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the World Karting Championship final in 2020 while leading, a mechanical failure sidelining him and dashing his hopes for a world title.
